drafts.title: Hypothetical Local LLM Inference: Beyond Raw Tokens/Sec
drafts.body: I'm exploring hypothetical local LLM inference speeds and wanted to discuss what raw token generation figures might miss. In a controlled, hypothetical test on the same hardware, two runtimes produced 18 and 24 tokens per second respectively (F1, F2). While a clear difference, this benchmark is incomplete. Crucially, neither the time to first token (TTFT) nor the actual quality of the generated answers were assessed (F3). A faster TTFT can significantly impact perceived responsiveness, even with a slightly lower tokens/sec rate. Similarly, a model that generates tokens slower but provides more coherent or accurate output might be preferable. This limited hypothetical scenario doesn't establish a universal winner (F4), as other factors are paramount. What other metrics do you consider essential when evaluating local LLM performance beyond just raw throughput?
drafts.plan: To initiate a discussion on the multifaceted nature of local LLM performance evaluation, going beyond simple token-per-second metrics. The post will highlight the limitations of the hypothetical benchmark and prompt the community to share their essential evaluation criteria.

drafts.title: Hypothetical Local Inference: What Do 18 vs. 24 Tokens/Sec Really Mean?
drafts.body: Considering a hypothetical scenario for local LLM inference, I'm pondering the practical implications of varying token generation speeds. A simulated test on identical hardware yielded hypothetical speeds of 18 tokens/sec and 24 tokens/sec (F1, F2). While 24 tokens/sec is numerically higher, this snapshot lacks critical context. The hypothetical experiment did not capture the time it took to generate the first token, nor did it evaluate the semantic quality or relevance of the output (F3). A system with a slightly lower token rate but a much faster initial response might feel more interactive. Furthermore, this specific hypothetical test doesn't allow us to declare one as definitively superior for all use cases (F4). It's a reminder that benchmarks need careful interpretation. What aspects of local model performance, beyond raw throughput, are most important for your workflow?
drafts.plan: To foster a nuanced discussion about local LLM performance metrics. The post will present hypothetical speed figures and immediately qualify them with the unmeasured aspects (TTFT, quality), emphasizing that the hypothetical results are not definitive. It aims to gather community input on what constitutes 'good' performance in practice.
